title: SparsePR: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation
hook: Skipping attention blocks in a video model is cheap; knowing what you threw away is the hard part. SparsePR partitions queries by response and then reconstructs the missing residual.
key_points: Training-free block-sparse attention speeds up video transformers, but knowing a row's attention is concentrated does not tell you which executable sparse operator to use.
Queries routed to the same block can have poorly overlapping supports, and retained attention mass alone does not predict post-softmax error from skipped interactions.
Response-Coupled Partitioning groups keys and values by sampled-query responses, using group centroids as query coordinates so co-routed queries actually share support.
Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction runs a few exact query rows per call and fits an affine correction that adds the dropped mass back into the sparse output.
Across four video generation and world models, SparsePR holds generation quality at 22-26% executed-pair density with 1.48x-2.61x end-to-end speedups.
Ablations attribute most of the error reduction to probe fitting; the partitioning mainly lowers hard-drop error under a small probe budget.
content_html: Training-free sparse attention is the cheap way to speed up video diffusion and world models: keep the heavy attention blocks, skip the rest, no retraining. Taghavi, Langari and Pandey argue the usual recipe is under-specified — observing that a query row's attention is concentrated doesn't tell you how to group queries into a routable block, and the attention mass you retain doesn't predict the post-softmax error from what you dropped.
extra_html:
SparsePR attacks both halves. Response-Coupled Partitioning builds K/V groups from how sampled queries actually respond, then uses the group centroids as coordinates so queries sharing a route also share support. Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction spends a small budget of exact query rows per call to fit an affine correction that pushes the skipped mass back into the sparse output, within the subspace the probe residuals expose.

Across four heterogeneous video generation and world models the authors report consistently lower attention-reconstruction error, preserved generation quality at 22.0-26.0% realized executed-pair density, and 1.48x-2.61x end-to-end speedups. Their ablations credit probe fitting with most of the gain. See the arXiv paper and project page for the full results.

related.title: MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA)
related.hook: Quadratic attention chokes at a million tokens. MiniMax runs exact attention over only a Top-k of key-value blocks per query group — cutting per-token attention compute ~28x at 1M context.

related.title: SANA-Video 2.0: Softmax Where It Counts
related.hook: Pure linear attention is cheap but loses full-rank token mixing. SANA-Video 2.0 sprinkles softmax anchors back in at a 3:1 ratio and reaches softmax-level video quality at linear-attention cost.

flashcards.prompt: Why isn't row-wise attention concentration enough to build a sparse attention operator?
flashcards.back_html: Concentration is per-row. Queries routed to the same block may have poorly overlapping supports, and retained attention mass alone does not determine the post-softmax error from the interactions you skipped.

flashcards.prompt: What does SparsePR's Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction actually do?

choices.text: Runs a few exact query rows and fits an affine correction to the sparse output
Fine-tunes the video model so it tolerates dropped attention blocks
Increases the block budget until reconstruction error falls below a threshold

flashcards.explanation_html: A small set of exact rows calibrates a call-specific affine correction inside the output subspace the probe residuals reveal — no retraining, and the sparsity budget stays fixed.

flashcards.prompt: Which of SparsePR's two components contributes most of the error reduction?
flashcards.back_html: Probe fitting. Ablations show the residual reconstruction accounts for most of the drop in attention-reconstruction error; response-coupled partitioning mainly reduces hard-drop error under a finite probe budget.
